passages.title: Shimmering Melodies
passages.text: This dust is of exceptional quality! Come, I will show you some techniques that make use of it.

passages.title: Shimmering Melodies
passages.text:
Have you heard it? The magic of Eversong. It emanates a subtle melody, if you listen closely enough. The complex interwoven strands of magic move against each other and create a beautiful harmony.

The dust distilled from such magic is exceptionally potent. Bring some to me and I will show you its uses.

passages.title: Shimmering Melodies
passages.text: Have you collected the dust?

passages.title: Splintered Radiance
passages.text: Oh, they glow with such wonderful power! These should do nicely.

passages.title: Splintered Radiance
passages.text:
When captured at just the right moment, the power exuding from an object can be crystallized into splinters of raw magical energy. The result is dazzling, like beams of sunlight splitting as they stream through a window.

Bring me some of these shards. My work cannot continue without them.

passages.title: Splintered Radiance
passages.text: A few shards should be sufficient.

passages.title: A Ray of Sunlight
passages.text: This will make many fine and powerful enchantments.

passages.title: A Ray of Sunlight
passages.text:
There is great magic in the dawn. It illuminates and awakens all it falls upon, rousing the land to action. It is potential in its purest form.

As enchanters, we can crystallize that potential. Bring a parcel of the dawn to me.

passages.title: A Ray of Sunlight
passages.text: Have you succeeded?

passages.title: Experience Tranquility
passages.text: Bless you. This will give me some extra time to catch up on orders.

passages.title: Experience Tranquility
passages.text:
Are you an herbalist? Oh, thank goodness.

I've found myself in need of an exorbitant amount of tranquility bloom. The orders from the alchemists keep piling up and I only just finished restocking our argentleaf and--

<Nathera stops to take a deep breath.>

Could you please bring me as much tranquility bloom as you can carry? I'd be in your debt.

passages.title: Experience Tranquility
passages.text: Have you found any tranquility bloom?

passages.title: Brittle and Brilliant
passages.text: I'll get these bundles hung up to dry at once. Thank you.

passages.title: Brittle and Brilliant
passages.text:
Argentleaf is always in high demand whenever war draws near.

It practically falls apart when you dry it out, but that powder can be used in a variety of medicines. It calms the nerves, focuses the mind, and can even work as a mild anesthetic in a pinch.

If you find any out in the field, please bring it to me.

passages.title: Brittle and Brilliant
passages.text: Argentleaf grows like a weed, to be honest. You should find plenty.

passages.title: The Root of Life
passages.text: Oh, I love the scent of fresh azeroot. Perhaps I should see how it would do in a perfume...

passages.title: The Root of Life
passages.text:
Most tuberous roots have some sort of healing potential, but azeroot is by far the most potent and versatile.

Just a small amount, juiced or powdered, can stave off infections, promote healing, and soothe both body and mind. I've even seen it used to keep lumber from rotting!

If you could bring me a few bushels, I'll put it to good use.

passages.title: The Root of Life
passages.text: Were you able to track down any azeroot?

passages.title: Sin'dorei Vices
passages.text: Excellent. With your help and what we already have in stock, this should cover his order.

passages.title: Sin'dorei Vices
passages.text:
While most of our harvests supply the scribes and alchemists in the city, we do occasionally receive orders from the public.

Lord Saltheril is one of our most prolific customers. He has an estate in western Eversong that he keeps well-supplied with offerings for guests at his soirees.

He has requested a large quantity of mana lilies and sanguithorn this week. Could you help us fulfill the order?

passages.title: Sin'dorei Vices
passages.text: Lord Saltheril's business is always welcome, even if a bit eccentric.

passages.title: Traditional Harvests
passages.text: Sometimes a simple blend is the best blend. No shame in sticking to the basics.

passages.title: Traditional Harvests
passages.text:
Tranquility bloom and argentleaf are the backbone of countless potions, elixirs, inks, and so much more.

It never hurts to keep a surplus around. If you find yourself with any extra, we would gladly take it off your hands.

passages.title: Traditional Harvests
passages.text: We'll take whatever you can offer.

passages.title: Copper for Your Thoughts?
passages.text: This is even more than I expected! Wonderful. I'll see this put to use immediately.

passages.title: Copper for Your Thoughts?
passages.text:
It's easy to overlook in favor of more extravagant materials, but copper is an extremely reliable and versatile material. Weapons, armor, wiring, jewelry, and of course the humble copper coin--it does it all!

Naturally, copper is always in high demand across the city and beyond. If you happen across any extra ore, I would gladly take it off your hands.

passages.title: Copper for Your Thoughts?
passages.text: You know, I wrote my thesis on the uses of copper. Have you read it?

passages.title: Aggressive Tin-dencies
passages.text:
Excellent! This will make a fine assortment of weapons.

I'm sure we'll get another order soon enough, so keep some spare tin around.

passages.title: Aggressive Tin-dencies
passages.text:
There's been an influx of newly recruited soldiers lately. Marvelous fighters in the making, but a little too enthusiastic. They've already done a number on the stock of training weapons.

We usually make training weapons out of tin or other soft metals. They keep the recruits from doing real damage to the training dummies or each other, but they don't last long.

We'll need a lot more tin than what we have in stock to keep up. Bring us some more!

passages.title: Aggressive Tin-dencies
passages.text: Anything you can contribute will be appreciated.

passages.title: It's Called Silvermoon
passages.text: What remarkable quality! I'll have this shipped over to the jewelers at once. Thank you.

passages.title: It's Called Silvermoon
passages.text:
Elegant gold filigree may be a favorite of the sin'dorei, but our city also boasts some of the finest silversmiths in Azeroth.

They have been receiving a particularly high number of orders with all of the new visitors passing through. If you come across any high-quality silver, they can put it to good use.

passages.title: It's Called Silvermoon
passages.text: I have a certain fondness for silver myself, truth be told.

passages.title: Conductive Metals
passages.text: Ah, yes. This quantity should be sufficient. I'll have it packaged up for the engineers.

passages.title: Conductive Metals
passages.text:
Our arcane constructs might look purely magical, but there's quite a bit of advanced wiring going on beneath the surface. Silvermoon's engineers truly are spell-workers in their own right.

They've been ramping up production lately to help fortify our defenses. Naturally, they look to us for supplies. I have most of the materials they ordered, but I'm low on tin and silver.

Could you help me fulfill the order?

passages.title: Conductive Metals
passages.text: Tin and silver are both remarkably conductive. I could elaborate, if you have a few hours?

passages.title: Stocking the Staples
passages.text:
You are one of the most reliable miners I've ever had the pleasure of meeting.

Thank you. Truly.

passages.title: Stocking the Staples
passages.text:
One can never have too much copper and thorium on hand. Even with all the new miners we brought on, we still nearly deplete our stocks every week.

At this rate, we'll have to start importing--and I do not want the headache that sort of paperwork brings.

If you could help us replenish our stock of copper and thorium, I would be in your debt.

passages.title: Stocking the Staples
passages.text: I suppose I could bring on a few more apprentices, if I have to...

passages.title: Tempered in Darkness
passages.text: What strange properties... I'll keep a sample for study. In the meantime, this leather will make fine armor for our Farstriders.

passages.title: Tempered in Darkness
passages.text:
The beasts of Quel'Thalas produce leather of unparalleled quality, but the Void has been doing something strange to it.

Normally, we harden leather by heating it under specific conditions. But the darkness clinging to these hides seems to be tempering the leather on its own. I have no idea how this is possible, but we can make use of it.

Bring me as much as you can gather. We have an army to supply.

passages.title: Tempered in Darkness
passages.text: We'll find a use for any leather you can bring us.

passages.title: The Chill of the Void
passages.text: Our leatherworkers should be able to use these materials. Nicely done.

passages.title: The Chill of the Void
passages.text:
When we mobilized troops to Northrend many years ago, we had to outfit our soldiers to withstand the icy chill of the frozen wastes. The secret is lining the inside of the armor with fur and plating it securely to trap warmth inside.

We kept detailed records of those techniques. The Void may not be as cold as Northrend, but I'd rather be prepared for the worst.

Bring me a supply of fur and plating and I'll see you compensated.

passages.title: The Chill of the Void
passages.text: As an added benefit, the fur prevents quite a bit of chafing.

passages.title: Style and Skill
passages.text: Ah, these should make excellent arrows.

passages.title: Style and Skill
passages.text:
In battle, appearances are nearly as important as raw skill. If you can intimidate your foe before you've even drawn your sword, you're already that much closer to victory.

Our fletchers take this a step further and insist that beautiful feathers make our Farstriders' arrows do more damage. I'm... not certain about that, but I can appreciate the aesthetic.

Here's a list of what they need for this week's batch of arrows. Supply whatever you can and I'll handle the rest.

passages.title: Style and Skill
passages.text: You can ignore the note about whether the feathers should be crimson or scarlet.

passages.title: Essential Materials
passages.text:
Well, this should be enough to cover the most recent order. I'll try to restock in preparation for the next one.

Pleasure working with you.

passages.title: Essential Materials
passages.text:
The Horde's penchant for teeth and animal pelts has worn off on some sin'dorei. It's not uncommon in recent years to receive bulk orders for both.

This is one of those times. If you have any spare hides, or come across any particularly sharp teeth in your hunts, I'd gladly trade you for them.

passages.title: Essential Materials
passages.text: I'll never understand orcish fashion.

passages.title: Minor Scales
passages.text: Oh, these are wonderful. Look at iridescence! I'll send these over at once.

passages.title: Minor Scales
passages.text:
A well-made suit of scalemail is a sight to behold. It requires quite a bit of patience and attention to fine detail, but Silvermoon's leatherworkers are masters of the craft.

If you happen to hunt any scaled beasts, we could use those materials. A large quantity of smaller sized ones, if you could--they layer more nicely in the armor.

passages.title: Minor Scales
passages.text: Scales are a bit harder to come by than regular leather, but the end result is well worth it.

passages.title: Learning the Cloaks - Part 1
passages.text:
You took to that like a cloak to concealment. Well done!

But, in this game, a good disguise or hiding spot isn't always enough. There is much more for you to learn.

passages.title: Learning the Cloaks - Part 1
passages.text:
In this game of Decor Duel, one side uses illusion to disguise themselves as, and hide amongst, everyday objects in the area.

The other side uses pre-approved lists of illusion-piercing abilities to find and then capture those hiding cloaked in disguise.

At the end of the round, the teams switch roles, so each side has a chance to hide and seek. 

Time for you to try! This armchair has been enchanted to cloak you with its disguise. Don its appearance, then change your disguise a few times.

passages.title: Learning the Cloaks - Part 1
passages.text: Touch this armchair, to don its disguise...

passages.title: Learning the Cloaks - Part 2
passages.text:
Nicely done! But that's only half the game, isn't it.

Next, let's get you exposed to some Capturing tactics. If you think you can handle it, of course.

passages.title: Learning the Cloaks - Part 2
passages.text:
When disguised, you will have the ability to magically teleport yourself to a nearby piece of decor.

Pick up the chair's disguise again, and this time try swapping your location a few times. Feel free to change your disguise between swaps if you'd like.

passages.title: Learning the Cloaks - Part 2
passages.text: Use the disguise chair to swap with other decor, then return to me.

passages.title: Nothing Captured, Nothing Gained
passages.text: Not bad for a first time. You're taking to this quite naturally!

passages.title: Nothing Captured, Nothing Gained
passages.text:
There are three Seeker classes in Decor Duel, but everyone starts off with the Spellbreaker kit. Don't worry--you can earn access to the others.

Some fundamentals: you can break the shield of a disguised hider's illusion by using Dispel Magic. Once the hider has been marked as Found, you'll have a brief window to Tag them, taking them out of the match.

My statue has been enchanted to outfit you with a Spellbreaker kit. Once outfitted, use Dispel Magic to find and tag decoys hiding around here.

passages.title: Nothing Captured, Nothing Gained
passages.text: Use my statue, then find and tag hiders with the Spellbreaker's Dispel Magic and Tag.

passages.title: Windrunner Spire
passages.text: It's as I thought... the spire houses more than just remnants of the Scourge. It's a mirror to the tragedies that befell the Windrunner family.

passages.title: Windrunner Spire
passages.text:
Former home of the Windrunners... now desecrated beyond thought. Since the Scourge invasion, the spire houses our greatest nightmares: banshees, abominations, hateful spirits.

There is no redeeming such a place, but perhaps we may help lay the tormented to rest.

passages.title: Murder Row
passages.text:
Well done thwarting such a massive operation.

Lor'themar will be relieved. Perhaps this will inspire him to enforce stricter measures in Murder Row.

passages.title: Murder Row
passages.text:
I've always disagreed with Lor'themar about the existence of Murder Row. But I guess like any forest, a city should and will have its secrets.

Though recently, Lor'themar has expressed concern about rising fel activity in the area. With the majority of Silvermoon's watch on the Voidstorm, many folks are testing boundaries, taking advantage, making a play for power...

You have my permission to investigate and crush any such illegal activities.

passages.title: Murder Row
passages.text: More reports of fel activity come in daily. Silvermoon is at risk, I fear. I hope you're on the case..

passages.title: Magisters' Terrace
passages.text: That was a close call. As for Rommath and Umbric, that's a puzzle for another day.

passages.title: Magisters' Terrace
passages.text:
Powerful monsters of the void have taken over Magister's Terrace! These halls contain untold amounts of knowledge and arcane power. We cannot lose any of it to our enemy.

Clear the voidspawns and their masters. You'll likely have to solve the terrace's defenses as well, which are designed to prevent and shutdown unauthorized access at any cost.

passages.title: Magisters' Terrace
passages.text: If the Void gains access to Silvermoon's most exclusive repository of magic... Rommath will throw a fit of epic proportions.

passages.title: Den of Nalorakk
passages.text: An incredible feat. You have my respect, champion.

passages.title: Den of Nalorakk
passages.text:
A trial of skill and strength... I'd go myself if I wasn't needed in Silvermoon.

Good luck, champion. I look forward to hearing about your victory against the Amani Loa of War.

passages.title: Den of Nalorakk
passages.text: Didn't chicken out, did you? It's okay, your fear is not unfounded. Bears are the kings of nature. They'll mess you up.

passages.title: The Blinding Vale
passages.text: Does this victory spell the death of the Lightbloom? Only time will tell. But in my experience, life always finds a way.

passages.title: The Blinding Vale
passages.text:
This place in Harandar is the Lightbloom's epicenter. Orweyna did what she could, which was much, but we must strike at the taproot of all roots for the plant to die.

Be on your guard, even if you think yourself experienced with the Lightbloom by now. The vale is different from the rampant, but ultimately wild growth in Eversong. It's a calculated force of nature led by a Rootwarden who seeks to strangle you and everything else it desires.

passages.title: The Blinding Vale
passages.text: Learn what you can from the Lightbloom in Eversong, but beware this may be an entirely different set of problems. The Rootwarden will be expecting intruders such as yourself.

passages.title: Voidscar Arena
passages.text: You've bested them all! Well done, champion. Maybe I'll sign up next time! It sounded like fun.

passages.title: Voidscar Arena
passages.text:
If I didn't know that the domanaar thirst for battle, and all the pain and strife that comes with it, I'd say this is trap. Either way, I suppose it's an invitation to get yourself killed.

If you insist on participating in the Void's fighting games, I can't stop you. Just don't hesitate to kill as many voidspawn as possible while you're there, okay?

passages.title: Voidscar Arena
passages.text: May your arrows strike true, champion.

passages.title: Nexus-Point Xenas
passages.text: Swift work, champion. It seems like we'll have to continue our routine inspections, but for now, we can rest.

passages.title: Nexus-Point Xenas
passages.text:
We must continue to keep an eye on this overpowered facility. If breached, disaster will spread beyond the Voidstorm. Unfortunately this magical and mechanical complex is beyond my area of expertise.

Prepare yourself, and ensure that the Nexus-Point Xenas remains dormant.

passages.title: Nexus-Point Xenas
passages.text:
If the Nexus-Point is overloaded, it'll be a very quick death for many.

Let's not entertain that thought any further. Secure the facility!

passages.title: Midnight: World Quests
passages.text: Well done. Together, our light will outshine the darkness the Void brings.

passages.title: Midnight: World Quests
passages.text:
The Void seeks to divide us, to drive a wedge between kin and kingdom alike. We cannot allow it.

Everywhere I turn, I hear of those struggling--families displaced, defenders overwhelmed, healers stretched thin. No blade nor spell alone will turn this tide, but the strength of many hearts united can.

Go forth and lend your aid where it is needed most.

passages.title: Midnight: World Quests
passages.text: With your aid, will can bring all our people closer together.

passages.title: Midnight: Housing
passages.text: You've given your heart. That is what truly unites us.

passages.title: Midnight: Housing
passages.text:
A strong community is built not by walls, but by the hands and hearts of those within it. 

Lend your voice, your time, and your spirit to the neighborhood. Help your fellows, share in their burdens, and take your place as an active part of the home we build together.

passages.title: When is a Chair not for Sitting?
passages.text: Greetings! Are you here to learn more about our joint venture?

passages.title: When is a Chair not for Sitting?
passages.text:
Aethas Sunreaver, Riftblade Maella, and Auric Sunchaser have recently revitalized an old arcane twist on hide and seek called Decor Duel.

They're looking for new participants to help spread the entertainment.

You should meet them over in Falconwing Square.

passages.title: Conditional - Multiple Objectives, Sequenced
passages.text:
I be sent out here ta prove dat I can be an amani warrior.

Dis trial needs me ta collect as many trophies from dese gnarldin as possible. 

De two of us should work together! I be helpin' you get recognized as an amani warrior, yeah?

Just go out dere and get as many trophies from de gnarldin as possible. 

I be stayin' behind ta watch our backs, eh?

passages.title: Conditional - Just One Objective
passages.text:
I be sent out here ta prove dat I can be an amani warrior.

Dis trial needs me ta collect as many trophies from dese gnarldin as possible. 

De two of us should work together! I be helpin' you get recognized as an amani warrior, yeah?

Just go out dere and get as many trophies from de gnarldin as possible. 

I be stayin' behind ta watch our backs, eh?

passages.title: A Gnawing Void of Curiosity
passages.text:
An extraordinary find. The arcane energies emanating from your discovery clearly predate the Shattering... We could learn much from such artifacts.

Champion! Fantastic work! If you happen upon any more during your expeditions, please bring your findings back to me.

passages.title: A Gnawing Void of Curiosity
passages.text: <The artifact crumbles in your hand, leaving only a faint but distinctly ancient arcane footprint. Naleidea Rivergleam will want to hear about this.>

passages.title: Blessings of the Loa
passages.text:
Ya spirit is flowing with strength!

You may use de altar as often as ya wish. But ya can only hold one blessing on ya self at a time.

passages.title: Blessings of the Loa
passages.text:
My name is Du'gal. And you are hash'ura.

Kinduru has ordered me to train you in de ways of loa worship. Take honor in it. Very few gokinye have earned de right as you have.

Beside me is de Altar of Blessings. You may use it to worship any of our loa, and you shall receive a sliver of power in thanks.

Go ahead now, if ya be so kind.

passages.title: Blessings of the Loa
passages.text: De loa are quite generous indeed.

passages.title: Putting it Together
passages.text:
Splendid! Well done out there, <name>!

You did well! And there are even more abilities and other Kits for you to discover and learn.

passages.title: Putting it Together
passages.text:
You have the basics now. All that's left is to experience the Arcane Propagator for yourself in a match of Decor Duel!

What is the Arcane Propagator, you ask? A mystic relic wrought from glamours. It lets players cloak themselves in the guise of enchanted objects.

We've partially recreated it with the chair for training, as you've seen, but the real thing is much better. Why not play a match for real right now?

passages.title: Putting it Together
passages.text:
<name>? No, I do not see your name on any of the game rosters.

\Speak with Gamemaster Fleurian to join a game of Decor Duel.

passages.title: Ghosts of the Ring
passages.text:
Who? Ah, I remember de priest now. He screamed very loudly when I tried to talk to him. It's been a while since I laughed dat hard.

You here to help?

passages.title: Ghosts of the Ring
passages.text:
I was at de Ring of Glory earlier. Have you been? De place is crawlin' with spirits and one of dem gave me quite de fright! Came right up and tried to talk to me! I was too nervous to stick 'round and find out what he wanted.

You look brave and strong. Maybe you oughta check it out.

passages.title: Bloom and Fade
passages.text:
Are dey not beautiful?

<He leans close, inhaling, but then sighs disappointedly.>

I cannot smell dem. I wish I could have, one more time. Hopefully Eshaye still can.

passages.title: Bloom and Fade
passages.text:
My time is runnin' out and I need to see if I can rescue my beloved, Eshaye. She's stuck in de loop, and I want to break her from de cycle before I fade entirely.

I used to be able to get through to her with bouquets of sweetsaw blooms. I can't grasp dem anymore, though. Will you gather some for me?

passages.title: Bloom and Fade
passages.text: I think de scent of de blooms always brought her back. I can't smell anything anymore. If she also can't, maybe nothing gonna bring her back.

passages.title: Ectoplasmic Extractions
passages.text: You done well. We are one step closer to breakin' Eshaye free from de loop.

passages.title: Ectoplasmic Extractions
passages.text:
Up near de Ring of Glory, there are spirits like myself who are merchants. Dey sell a variety of things to other spirits, but I got Eshaye's attention in de past using a beverage from Mab'jul.

De market goods can be purchased with ectoplasm, which can be gathered from de frayed spirits around de Ring. Especially de cultists, who steal it from de others.

passages.title: Ectoplasmic Extractions
passages.text:
At first, we just wandered in de swamp: confused, angry, hurtin', scared. After many thousands of years, some learned how to transmute de ectoplasm left behind when another spirit is sundered. Dis currency began to be quite sought after.

You cannot destroy a spirit here entirely. Eventually, it will reform itself, but it takes a very long time. Since none of us can move on, there's always a supply of ectoplasm, though gatherin' is difficult. Were you able to procure enough?

passages.title: Ectoplasmic Emporium
passages.text: I see. Been too long since I last gave her flowers. Her memory of dem, and of our time together, may be long gone.

passages.title: Ectoplasmic Emporium
passages.text:
Eshaye is sure to love these flowers! Now all we need is de spectral brew. Take de ectoplasm to Mab'jul and exchange it for a bottle of spectral brew.

It's a vintage made from harvested ectoplasm, and is quite refreshing. It sometimes has de ability to stall fraying.

passages.title: Ectoplasmic Emporium
passages.text: I remember de first time I gave her flowers. I didn't think a warrior like her could blush, but she did. I hope I never forget her smile dat day.

passages.title: Communing with Ghosts
passages.text:
Challenge Eshaye? Of course! Why didn't I think of dat?

Erm, probably because I can't beat her.

passages.title: Communing with Ghosts
passages.text:
Dat was a long shot, but I still wanted to try.

<He pauses a moment and shudders, seeming to flicker at the edges.>

I am out of ideas, <name>. Will you ask around? Some of de others here may have some ideas of how to get through to Eshaye. I am not welcome too close to dem, or I would come with you.

passages.title: Lost Iridescent Flightstone
passages.text: A relic of a time passed. It glimmers with the shine of all of the dragonflights, a solemn reminder of the beauty and strength when we come together.

passages.title: Lost Iridescent Flightstone
passages.text:
The flightstone glimmers with the colors of all aspects. Within the glittering light you have visions of noble dragon houses locked in battle against Primal Incarnates. A vicious cacophony of roars as Shadowflame consumes swaths of land. And the soothing sounds of nature as a world tree blooms.

The soaring skies of Valdrakken call.

passages.title: The Ephemeron Masquerade
passages.text: Ah, well done! I watched you out there, and it was quite thrilling!

passages.title: The Ephemeron Masquerade
passages.text:
The deeds of today becomes the tales of dusk!

Seekers and Hiders, alike, make their mark through thrilling game play and strategic out maneuvering.

The sun shines its light on a new day, shattering the illusions of yesterday, and elongating the shadows of today. Are you ready?

Don you disguise, secure your kit, and show your peers no one can hold a candle to you ... literally!

passages.title: The Ephemeron Masquerade
passages.text: Your task remains incomplete, <name>.

passages.title: Conditional Objectives - Sequential
passages.text:
<name>! Glad to see you. The defenders in the fortress could use your help.

One of the gnomes built a robot to try to help defend the keep. However, it goes haywire every time it turns on.

She needs the help of someone who can properly disrupt the robot's attacks so it can be repaired.

Do you have a moment to help?

passages.title: Conditional Objectives - Multiple Steps, No Sequence
passages.text:
<name>! Glad to see you. The defenders in the fortress could use your help.

One of the gnomes built a robot to try to help defend the keep. However, it goes haywire every time it turns on.

She needs the help of someone who can properly disrupt the robot's attacks so it can be repaired.

Do you have a moment to help?

passages.title: Conditional Objectives - Conditional After Sequence
passages.text:
<name>! Glad to see you. The defenders in the fortress could use your help.

One of the gnomes built a robot to try to help defend the keep. However, it goes haywire every time it turns on.

She needs the help of someone who can properly disrupt the robot's attacks so it can be repaired.

Do you have a moment to help?

passages.title: Midnight: Abundance
passages.text: You have met the Loa of Abundance. May its gifts serve you well.

passages.title: Midnight: Abundance
passages.text:
The trolls of Zul'Aman draw their strength from the loa: ancient spirits that grant power to those who honor them. These boons can be wondrous or perilous, depending on the loa's nature and the devotion of its followers.

There are whispers of a Loa of Abundance dwelling within Zul'Aman, its blessings said to bring prosperity to those deemed worthy.

Seek it out, learn what drives it, and see if its favor would serve our cause.

passages.title: Midnight: Legends of the Haranir
passages.text: You have seen what the Zur'ashar preserved. Through their living art, the past speaks still.

passages.title: Midnight: Legends of the Haranir
passages.text:
For the Haranir, art is a language of memory. 

Their history endures not in words but in vivid stories painted upon stone with pigments imbued with power. Through these works, the Zur'ashar, their revered historians, entwine living visions of the past to the present. Each vision draws us deeper into the haranir's mysteries, guiding us closer to the truths that shaped their world.

passages.title: Midnight: Stormarion Assault
passages.text:
The Citadel stands as proof of what we can achieve together. 

Against unity, even the Void itself must yield.

passages.title: Midnight: Stormarion Assault
passages.text:
The fight against Xal'atath tests our resolve, but it will not break us.

Void anomalies twist the halls of Stormarion Citadel, but they will find no weakness here. The Void Elves stand as our allies. Prove to our enemies that our strength when united is beyond the reach of even the Void.

Go, <name>--aid them, and see the Citadel cleansed of corruption.

passages.title: Slayer's Rise
passages.text: <name>, you made it through. Well done.

passages.title: Slayer's Rise
passages.text: We've received reports of escalated troubles between some domanaar. Go investigate the battle in Slayer's Rise, then report to Deminos Darktrance in Masters' Perch.

passages.title: Defying Gravity
passages.text:
Now, we descend. The Void energy below is unlike any I've felt before, as if gravity itself yields to the Void. Once you enter the cave, its influence will be upon you.

Kalgorg has already slain and claimed power from the creatures within. Their violent deaths have left behind some kind of cursed terrain. But we must proceed and claim the power within. Fill the reliquary to the brim. 

I know not what to expect from my voidwalker. We will need all the power we can manage.

passages.title: Ongoing Stoppage
passages.text:
The Shadowguard may once have defied Xal'atath, but they're part of her army now. Whatever they're doing with the energies gathered here must be stopped.

Put down their soldiers, harvesters, and machines. I'll do the same, and meet you deeper within.

passages.title: Untethering the Two
passages.text:
Thank you for snapping me out of dat cycle, <name>. All I could remember was seeking victory on de day we were killed. I didn't remember what I was fighting for: to return to Ja'bonu and de life we shared.

I feel complete and whole for de first time in thousands of years. Whatever it was dat trapped us here, it cannot hold me and Ja'bonu any longer. We can move on now, to de next adventure, together.

passages.title: Untethering the Two
passages.text:
It never occurred to me to attack Eshaye. I been wasting time tryin' to get her to talk to me, without knowin' how to talk to her.

Will you do dis for me? Challenge Eshaye and beat her. Could dis wake her up? I feel hope stirrin'.

passages.title: Edification of the Worthy
passages.text: Excellent! Great work, <name>. Don't forget to check in often! You'll want to make sure you unlock the full potential of all the Kits available in order to maximize your enjoyment--and points-earning potential, of course.

passages.title: Edification of the Worthy
passages.text:
When you acquire a new Seeker kit, it always starts off relatively lean.

But you'll earn Illusionary Coins as you play, and may trade them in with Gamemaster Fleurian for expanded abilities, and even additional kits!

Take these. Add them to what you earned and demonstrate your shopping prowess.

passages.title: Edification of the Worthy
passages.text: Those coins were a one-time gift, <name>. If you have mislaid them, or have suffered the misfortune of thievery, then I suppose you will have to enter the games to collect more.

passages.title: Midnight: Prey
passages.text: Astalor serves Silvermoon's cause, though his path to that end is rarely a straight one.

passages.title: Midnight: Prey
passages.text:
Silvermoon is beset on all sides by threats both known and unknown. There are those who seek to track these threats and put an end to the strife and chaos they create.

Speak with Magister Astalor Bloodsworn in Murder Row. He will guide you toward the urgent threats.

passages.title: Midnight: Raid
passages.text:
You've faced the darkness and emerged stronger.

Well done, <name>.

passages.title: Midnight: Raid
passages.text:
Gather your allies, you will face the great trials ahead. 

The rewards are vast, and can aid you in the battles ahead. You and your allies need only vanquish a small number of these terrible foes.

passages.title: Midnight: Raid
passages.text: Hold fast, champion.

passages.title: Midnight: World Boss
passages.text: May your victories light the path for all who follow.

passages.title: Midnight: World Boss
passages.text:
Powerful enemies roam Azeroth, their strength growing with each passing battle.

Only through courage and unity will you emerge victorious.

passages.title: Midnight: World Boss
passages.text: Do not waver, <name>.

passages.title: The War Within Recap
passages.text: <The tome floats in front of you. Its pages are filled with knowledge of all that has happened.>

passages.title: The War Within Recap
passages.text:
<A parchment reaches you from an unknown sender.>

<It speaks of perusing a tome to catch up on current events, and how it is vital to understand a looming threat.>

<Perhaps you should seek out this tome to understand more when you are ready.>

passages.title: Courting Success
passages.text: I half expected you to run back home in tears! I hope you had a stunning time.

passages.title: Courting Success
passages.text:
You seek an audience with Saltheril? And you're wearing... that? Excuse me for a moment while I laugh into my handkerchief.

<Caeris laughs lightly behind his handkerchief.>

Now, let me be professional. You are cordially invited to attend Saltheril's soiree.

Don't embarrass yourself, <name>. The best of Silvermoon are watching.

passages.title: An Abundance of Wealth
passages.text:
Heh! So ya finally met Dundun.

Even de smallest are some of de greatest among de loa!

passages.title: An Abundance of Wealth
passages.text:
De Loa of Abundance may not be one of de four great ones, but his worshippers are certainly de most devout.

Seek him out yaself. You can find him in northern Zul'Aman near Halazzi's Temple, but I also hear he's established harvest sites in Eversong Woods, Harandar, and even de land of Void through de gargantuan skymouth.

If nothing else, de rewards he grants are glorious--to de worthy, at least.

passages.title: An Abundance of Wealth
passages.text: Did you find de loa, hash'ura?

passages.title: Guarded Treasures
passages.text: Well done, <name>.

passages.title: Guarded Treasures
passages.text:
Our sojourn to this world has brought the ren'dorei an even deeper understanding of the Void than before. The domanaar with whom we share a common enemy are almost strangely generous with their knowledge. I believe they want us to become as fearsome as they are.

There is a Singularity Anchor in Stormarion Citadel. I have learned how to draw upon some of its power to craft you a powerful item.

But first, we must ensure it does not fall into the hands of our enemies.

passages.title: Guarded Treasures
passages.text: Have you defended the anchor from the encroaching void forces?

passages.title: Spark of Radiance
passages.text:
This is a Spark of Radiance.

Every week, one of these sparks will appear while on your adventures. In its current state, it's rather useless, but acquiring more will allow you to craft powerful items. Reagents like these are malleable, robust, and the prize for many crafters.

This is a unique crafting material that can help an item achieve expertise beyond that of mortal ability.

passages.title: Spark of Radiance
passages.text:
A vision of radiance permeates your mind.

Eldara Dawnrunner might have more information regarding these Sparks of Radiance.

passages.title: Ancient Curiosity: Combat
passages.text: <You hold the curio and discover a shimmering glow emanating from it. This looks important.>

passages.title: Ancient Curiosity: Utility
passages.text: <You hold the curio and discover a shimmering glow emanating from it. This looks important.>

passages.title: Call Shot
passages.text:
Critters of all kind are crawling around Eversong and beyond. Cute, cuddly, creepy--whatever strikes your fancy.

Ya might be used to havin' varmints bash heads until one was weak enough to nab. Got a new way to try. All you need is a crate. You've got one, yeah?

Just throw the crate from the start. It's mighty effective, I tell ya.

You look tough enough to nab your own. Why don't ya give it a try?

passages.title: Bones of My Soul
passages.text: Gral's power, my soul... it's all here again. Thank you for returnin' my bones, <name>.

passages.title: Bones of My Soul
passages.text:
Do you have time to break a curse, <class>?

I'm what remains of a loa speaker of Gral. I kept de prisoners in line on Gral's Belly. But we crashed, I died, and de prisoners escaped.

My powers didn't work on de livin' anymore. But they did work on de captain, who'd died with me.

Terrified of his anger at my failure, I set up a ritual to trap him in de ship using my own bones.

My soul has leeched into de bones after all this time, and now I can't move them. Would you bring my bones to me?

passages.title: Bones of My Soul
passages.text:
This ritual was an odd one my teacher taught me a long, long time ago.

I never thought I'd need to perform rituals as a ghost, but I couldn't imagine how angry de captain would become.

passages.title: Meat for the Bones
passages.text: Perfect, perfect! You got enough meat there for these old bones.

passages.title: Meat for the Bones
passages.text:
To move my soul out o' de bones and into me, I need to do a ritual.

Gral is de loa of many things, but mostly de sea. He's a shark. And he likes meat!

Get meat from de sea creatures around here. It will be easier to perform de ritual with somethin' red and oozing to ground me.

passages.title: Meat for the Bones
passages.text: Plenty of loa speakers of Gral use meat in their rituals. Movin' my soul out o' de bones will take a lot of meat. But I'm sure that's nothing to you, right <class>?

passages.title: One Final Prisoner
passages.text: You've dispelled one of two ghosts keepin' this curse going. I thank you.

passages.title: One Final Prisoner
passages.text:
I cannot pretend I am any better than de captain.

We both enjoyed lording our power over de prisoners. When he'd lash out, I did not stop him.

But in our time trapped here together, I've reflected. De minute I wasn't useful to him, he got angry. And now I want this to end.

I cannot enable him any more. Would you put him to rest?

passages.title: Meat and Bone and Soul
passages.text:
You've helped me a lot, <name>. Thank you.

Now all this can end.

passages.title: Meat and Bone and Soul
passages.text:
We have everything we need for de ritual.

Meet me at de Tooth o' Sargoth. You'll help me get my soul back in one piece, then this curse will finally be over.

May Gral judge me on de other side for my failures here.

passages.title: Meat and Bone and Soul
passages.text: Just a few more steps. Need de bones tossed and de water chummed and then my soul will be in one piece again.

passages.title: The Gloves Are Off
passages.text:

Use your Blood-Soaked Invitation first then talk to a Bouncer in the Brawlpub and get to brawling!

passages.title: Ranger Captain's Summons
passages.text:
One threat may be dealt with, but dangers from all sides continue to stir within our borders.

A domanaar highlord rallies the minions of the Void to fill the vacuum of power.

Strange ethereals and their machines encroach on our settlements.

Even the remnants of the Twilight's Blade and local naga tribes have been emboldened by the chaos.

We could use your expertise in dealing with these threats, and I have just the task to get you started.

passages.title: Ranger Captain's Summons
passages.text:
Pardon the intrusion, <name>!

I'm delivering a summons from Ranger Captain Lilatha. She's requested your presence at her staging grounds overlooking the Bazaar near the north gate of Silvermoon.

Our lands are once again under threat and we'll need all the support we can get.

Report to her when you can!

passages.title: Outfitting and Allies
passages.text:
What did you think of our troll ally? It galls me to work with forces who attacked our lands in the past to defend them now. The enemy of my enemy I suppose. 

I will respect her prowess though--she looks like she can hold her own in a fight. Time will tell if she is worthy of my admiration or my ire.

passages.title: Outfitting and Allies
passages.text:
Halduron Brightwing has made sure that our task force is well equipped to handle any threat. I want you to check in with our quartermaster, Maren Silverwing. She will help you get outfitted. 

I also want you to talk with our "liaison." She is the troll with the guards. You may already know we are not alone in being targeted. 

Brightwing has reminded us that these enemies do not respect borders, so threats to Zul'Aman require our attention just as much as Eversong. We must deal with the troll.

passages.title: Outfitting and Allies
passages.text: When you have time continue to talk with others in our task force. We are prepared to support all of your efforts!

passages.title: Ritual Problems
passages.text:
I hope you now respect the dangers posed by great rituals. 

I fear though that these sites have the potential to be an even greater danger as we investigate them more and new challenges present themselves.

passages.title: Ritual Problems
passages.text:
To get right to it, I have laid out some lessons and some scout objectives for us as we approach the various dangers we might see in these ritual sites.

I have also marked on your map the location of one of these rituals. Take care, as the magics we have seen woven at these sites can overwhelm even the most stalwart warrior.

passages.title: Ritual Problems
passages.text: Were you successful?

passages.title: Ritual Interest
passages.text:
Kul'amara is such a fascinating individual. Did you know she fights on the front lines while also studying a multitude of rituals? It's such an incongruity and I love it.

Are you ready to stop these rituals that Kul'amara has warned us about?

passages.title: Ritual Interest
passages.text:
I am here at the behest of the great Zul'jarra! May she lead her people to greatness.

We face dire threats. Your Captain General is focused on the martial stakes, but the terrible magics unleashed recently pose an even greater danger. Our scouts have discovered rituals that risk ruin for us all.

Your Ranger Captain has recruited the Lady Darkglen, who appears to be a knowledgeable and capable ritual expert.

Seek her out in the tent nearby to find out how best to approach these ritual sites.

passages.title: Void Assaults: Eversong Woods
passages.text:
I knew you were key to our efforts and the right person to counter these threats! We face a diverse group of enemies, so someone who can react to new situations will continue to excel among our ranks.

I look forward to working with you on our next assignment, but stay vigilant! These threats do not show signs of waning.

passages.title: Void Assaults: Eversong Woods
passages.text: We are seeing a Void Assault in Eversong. We need you to head out immediately to counter these threats. I will mark the strikes on your map as our scouts identify them and direct your efforts from here.

passages.title: Void Assaults: Eversong Woods
passages.text: We must stay vigilant!

passages.title: Void Assaults: Zul'Aman
passages.text:
The Ranger Captain's faith in you is well earned. My people are also indebted to you for your assistance. 

I look forward to working with you again. My scouts do say that strikes still continue, so stay vigilant out there.

passages.title: Void Assaults: Zul'Aman
passages.text:
My scouts report a Void Assault in Zul'Aman. We need your help to counter these threats. 

I will direct you, and my scouts will continue to mark new activities on your map.

passages.title: Void Assaults: Zul'Aman
passages.text: We will triumph over these foes!

passages.title: Down a Peg
passages.text:
Truly, I am incredibly talented!

<Tytalor appears to be lost within his own thoughts.>

passages.title: Down a Peg
passages.text:
There seems to be a problem student at the academy.

I have heard reports that a student, Tytalor Goldenblade, is stirring up trouble in Sunstrider Isle. I'd go myself but I have my hands full running practice here already.

Could you go check on him and... educate him of his misgivings?

passages.title: Crest Transmutation
passages.text:
Remarkable!

Keep in mind I can only transmute crests into a higher tier when you have outgrown their usefulness, and it will be a costly process. Thank you for all of your help, <name>!

passages.title: Crest Transmutation
passages.text:
Did you know that crests can be transmuted into different tiers?

If you find yourself with crests that are too powerful for the gear you've acquired, I can help you transmute those crests into lower tiers that you can use.

And once all of your gear is sufficiently powerful, I'll be able to transmute your spare lower crests into higher ones!

Let's practice the transmutation process. Here's a few Veteran Dawncrests. Speak to me and I can transform them into Adventurer Dawncrests for you.

passages.title: Crest Transmutation
passages.text: If you lose those Veteran Dawncrests, you can find more from powerful creatures around Eversong, Zul'Aman, Harandar, and Voidstorm. I've heard there's quite a variety of them!

passages.title: Sanctum Secure
passages.text:
Our control here is only the beginning. Xal'atath has left other pockets of anomalies across the land. The defenses we've devised here can be used to secure those areas as well.

Travel to Sunkiller Sanctum and construct five additional defenses to solidify our hold on that location.

I will supply the Stormarion Core necessary to activate those defenses.

passages.title: Ophidia the Broodmother
passages.text:
Wa'kani may have blundered dis mission, but she was right to have you defeat de egg-layer. Dis is a significant blow to de expansion plans of de Children of Ula'tek here in de mire.

Ndamu and de other scouts remain missing, however. I fear de murlocs have them.

passages.title: Ophidia the Broodmother
passages.text:
Zawadi safe, eh? Good. No harm should come to her. We need to deal with these oversized worms.

Just over there, by de beach, is one of their broodmothers. Vile creature! Responsible for all de eggs you see 'round here. Kill her. Their invasion will stall, giving my people more time to organize a strike.

I need to tend my wounds. I will hide and wait for you.

passages.title: Home at Last
Midnight: Battlegrounds
passages.text: You've returned with the fire of battle in your eyes.

passages.title: Midnight: Battlegrounds
passages.text:
Battlegrounds stand as crucible where soldiers clash for honor, resources, and glory.

Each victory hones your skill and strengthens your resolve.

Go, test yourself against worthy foes and bring pride to your banner.

passages.title: Heritage of the Haranir
passages.text:
You have seen many battles and met many peoples. Your journeys continue to bring us closer to the wisdom and grace of Aln'hara. 

Since you left, roots and vines began to rapidly grow within your old home. Eventually, their purpose became clear: armor, grown for you from the roots of the great trees as a blessing from Aln'hara herself!

Wear it with pride as you continue your journey, <name>. Thank you.

passages.title: Heritage of the Haranir
passages.text:
You have travelled far and learned much of Aln'hara's grace.

It is time to return home and share the wisdom you have earned with your people.

passages.title: The Great Vault
passages.text:
Has the vault bestowed a fine relic upon you? Excellent!

The vault's splendor is often replenished. Keep your visits frequent, <name>. Fortune favors those who return.

passages.title: The Great Vault
passages.text:
In wake of recent events, the Vanguard of the Light has recovered and preserved relics of exceptional power and craftsmanship. To safeguard these treasures from prying eyes, the Magisters of Silvermoon have conjured a vault within Silvermoon's bank.

Only the most proven of champions may earn the right to draw from its splendor. If the Light deems you worthy, you may be bestowed an artifact of great power.

passages.title: The Great Vault
passages.text: The Light favors you, and so too does the vault. Look within.

passages.title: The Voidspire: Flicker in the Hollow
passages.text: Do not stray into the shadows, <name>--I cannot guarantee your safety.

passages.title: The Voidspire: Flicker in the Hollow
passages.text:
There's little light in these lands. What remains is fractured, hidden, or fading.

Fetch me Echoes of Radiance and I will grant you passage where no path should exist.

passages.title: What Hope in the Light?
passages.text:
Ever since the terrible events of the Voidspire, Arator has suffered. He has kept to himself, or prayed alone at the Dawnwell.

We all feel the loss of Alleria and Turalyon, but Arator only reunited with them recently, after their long fight against the Burning Legion.

I worry that if he is left to his own thoughts for too long, he may not come out of this the same.

Let us go to the Dawnwell and check on him.

passages.title: Resurgence in Deatholme
passages.text:
While we cannot know yet where Xal'atath has gone, or if Alleria and Turalyon are still alive, we can still pursue information.

Riftblade Maella has kept me up to date on the Twilight cultists. They have been gathering strength, gathering numbers, and seem to be searching for... something. Now is the time to act.

Let us travel to the Ruins of Deatholme and see why the cultists there have reinvigorated themselves.

passages.title: The Direct Method
passages.text:
The information we need has to be here! We just need to get it from the Twilight's Blade.

There's nothing wrong with the direct method. Apply force, and see what you can learn.

I brought Benthar's Scarlet Spire, the relic we rescued from the Scarlet Crusade. It's already been used to help protect the Sunwell, and maybe it can help us here.

passages.title: They Always Write It Down
passages.text:
An organization as widespread and diverse as the Twilight's Blade must need to write down their objectives.

Or at the least, whatever they have collected should shed light on what they're up to. 

See if you can find anything that points to their current direction.

passages.title: My Poor Beautiful Self
passages.text:
Oh, please don't hurt me!

<The pathetic voidling cowers at the sight of you.>

It's not my fault. I could have gotten them out of this.

It's those new commanders! They have led the Twilight cult down the wrong path.

Glaivh is the worst of them. If he was gone, perhaps, perhaps...

passages.title: Under New Management
passages.text:
The rank-and-file Twilight's Blade didn't have much to tell us, but their new leadership may know more.

You've already bested one of them. Let's see if there are others who also aspire to lead, and learn what they know.

You can still use the Scarlet Spire on them. If Umbric won't use his magic, then perhaps the Light will make them talk.

They should be below us, in the chasm.

passages.title: A Comeback Story
passages.text:
No one notices a creature like me...

No one appreciates how much I have lost.

But in that underestimation... knowledge.

Help me regain some strength, and I will regain the words you need.

passages.title: Verifiably Untrustworthy
passages.text:
As soon as we met that little voidling, I thought there was something I recognized. 

How Antenorian survived, I know not. But it's clear that we cannot let him get away. We need to know what he knows, and then his time on Azeroth should truly be ended.

Come, let's get what we need and finish this.

passages.title: Null Space
passages.text:
Arator jumped after Antenorian like a man possessed. He's so blinded by this crusade, he... he must not know how dangerous it is for someone like him to simply leap into the Void blindly.

No, we must think calmly about this. Analyze the situation.

We have no way of knowing what's on the other side of that portal. 

But we must go in. We must find Arator.

passages.title: Carving Out Room
passages.text:
I need a moment, after what we just went through. I feel like my body is fighting with itself.

But we're in hostile territory. I can't let us fall to enemies just because I was... because I had to jump in after him. We need to keep Umbric safe.

Can you clear out the Twilight's Blade around us to give us some room to recover?

passages.title: A Dark Shadow Looms
passages.text:
We are lucky to have survived that tear through the Void, but now we are presented with an opportunity.

Antenorian must have been going somewhere in this direction, which is why we find ourselves no longer in Eversong. But we interrupted his journey, and he is still here somewhere.

I can feel it like a chill along my spine.

See if you can find any more information from the Twilight's Blade here. What of that gateway that Antenorian spoke of? What of those Amani prophecies?

passages.title: The Call of the Void
passages.text:
I've been able to trace where Antenorian fled. He is more powerful than he was before, after that jaunt through the void space. 

Fortunately, this makes him easy to track. He's below us, in an open cavity underground. I can open a portal there.

<Umbric glances over at Arator.>

I hope that we can put an end to this, and Arator is no worse for wear. When we started this, I thought we would find a few scrolls, uncover their plan, and put a stop to it ourselves.

I did not anticipate this.

passages.title: Like Mother, Like Son
passages.text:
<Arator quietly seethes.>

We need to tell Lor'themar what we've learned. Not because I want to stop looking for Xal'atath, but this is important.

Come, let's leave Zul'Aman and return to Silvermoon.

You are one stylish <class>.

passages.title: Building the Voidforge
passages.text: Ah, the nascent Voidforge is ready! Oh the things I... I mean we, will be able to do with this...

passages.title: Building the Voidforge
passages.text:
I have been considering how I may offer you greater strength, my friend. I've come up with something, but I need your help building a proper Voidforge.

What? Oh, fear not, all my ulterior motives are still aligned with your cause. For now.

To begin, I need one Elementary Voidcore. You will be able to find shards from the more powerful foes you habitually encounter. Inflict your usual violence, return the shards, and I can weave them back into a true Voidcore to serve as the forge's foundation.

passages.title: Research Console: Exploring the Void
passages.text: More samples, excellent! The console hungers...

passages.title: Research Console: Exploring the Void
passages.text:
No rest for the researchers, as they say.

As much as I would love to go traipsing around this blasted voidscape, I need to remain at this post. But you! You can be our eyes and ears in the abyss.

Go and explore the Voidstorm, maybe we can find some additional samples to feed into the console.

passages.title: Research Console: Exploring the Void
passages.text: Back so soon?

passages.title: Curing Curse Resistance
passages.text:
<Second Mate Sluggs stares at the fish livers with wide eyes.>

O-oh, thank you, <name>! Captain Tokka will... really like those.

You can set them down there. Thank you. Truly.

passages.title: Curing Curse Resistance
passages.text:
Now that the Hoarder is gone, the fish population has boomed. There's a flood of fish with no curse at all!

Captain Tokka wants to study these curse-resistant fish. Go and collect a few of their livers so we can see what keeps them swimming.

If we want to use the venom-curse for ourselves, we need more cursed fish!

passages.title: Curing Curse Resistance
passages.text: Captain Tokka is always experimenting with something. He keeps jars of cursed fish guts. H-he's sure to like whatever you find, <name>!

passages.title: Ssak'mozek's Desire
passages.text:
<Second Mate Sluggs shakes with excitement.>

The lure worked! Just like Captain Tokka showed me. And it's all thanks to you.

We have more work to do, <name>, but you should take a moment to celebrate your victory. Until tomorrow!

passages.title: Ssak'mozek's Desire
passages.text:
Captain Tokka finished the lure for Ssak'mozek. It's time to kill the beast!

Take the lure into the marsh, near the wreck of Pa'ku's Talon. Ready yourself, then place it on the rocks there.

Ssak'mozek will be drawn to the lure. Kill it.

passages.title: Crushed Crabs
passages.text:
I'll take these to Captain Tokka so we can get the traps put back together.

The Hoarder may be reducing our food supply on several fronts, but he'll never understand the curse like Captain Tokka!

passages.title: Crushed Crabs
passages.text:
Hegvosh the Hoarder is back!

He's already started killing anything that gets in his way. This time, he's stomped on all of our crab traps in the south.

Salvage any working trap pieces you find. We'll need to rebuild them.

passages.title: Crushed Crabs
passages.text: We trap crabs for food, mostly. Even Captain Tokka needs to eat! He also likes to create new and, uh, interesting ways to trap the crabs. Mostly using venom-cursed needles.

passages.title: Death from the Dead
passages.text: See how the beads shine without any light hitting them? Ssak'mozek will be able to see this from far underwater. Smells, sight... two pieces of the lure ready to go.

passages.title: Death from the Dead
passages.text:
Ssak'mozek always has three heads. Captain Tokka's lure targets each of them.

The next piece of the lure is ethereal beads from ghosts on the Isle. They exist somewhere between here and the beyond and shine in just the right way that the hydra can't ignore them.

Ye can find some of these beads in the Crypt of the Lost Mason. Be careful--the ghosts may not like you entering that place.

passages.title: Death from the Dead
passages.text: Captain Tokka likes to say "there's no taboos in venom fishin'." He's right of course! But if you maybe have concerns about sort of robbing graves, I've dug around in that crypt over and over again. The beads are more ghost than real artifact.

passages.title: Going for the Crown
passages.text: That's everything we need. I'll craft the lure. Next, we take down that monster!

passages.title: Going for the Crown
passages.text:
The final pieces of Captain Tokka's hydra lure are feathers from the Children of Ula'tek themselves.

Ssak'mozek is trained to listen to the orders of these monsters. It lies in wait for them to call it from the murky depths. The lure can't work without something tying it to Ssak'mozek's masters.

Any of the children at the Gate of the Eastern Fang will have feathers perfect for the lure. Bring as many as you can.

passages.title: Going for the Crown
passages.text: Do you have the last piece of Ssak'mozek's lure? We need feathers--the brighter, the better.

passages.title: A Collection of Rot
passages.text: You've slain the Hoarder! We have a window to fish our fill, thanks to you. You should get back out there!

passages.title: A Collection of Rot
passages.text:
Have you noticed fewer fish on the south side of Atal'Utek lately? That's the Hoarder at work.

He's this big ugly sea giant we can't seem to shake. You'll know you've found him when you see piles of dead fish rotting away.

Make him think twice about taking too much from these waters.

passages.title: The New Hoard, Poached
passages.text: I could hear the angry hissing from here, <name>! Hopefully the Children of Ula'tek will stay away from our fishing spot for a while.

passages.title: The New Hoard, Poached
passages.text:
The Children of Ula'tek eat venom-cursed fish straight from the water. Now that we've made the fish stronger, the children have gone into a feeding frenzy!

Captain Tokka says to stop the poaching. The children have plenty of venom already!

passages.title: Wriggling and Wet
passages.text: These will do excellent! Ssak'mozek lurks beneath the water. The smell from these leech legs will help draw it to you.

passages.title: Wriggling and Wet
passages.text:
Captain Tokka wants us to fish for Ssak'mozek.

The Children of Ula'tek raise a hydra more vicious and venom-cursed than all the rest. We've caught and killed it before, but they always raise another and give it the same name: Ssak'mozek.

We're going to craft one of Tokka's best lures to draw it in.

Start by collecting the legs of leeches. When broken, they have a smell the children and their creations cannot resist.

passages.title: Wriggling and Wet
passages.text: Don't break the leech legs, if you can. We need to break them right before we make the lure so the smell is fresh.
