passages.text:
Ah, an Idol of Abundance.

De lord of glory and plentitude must favor you highly above his many other acolytes.

passages.title: Blessings of Abundance
passages.text:
<This idol proves the depth of your bond with abundance.

Speak with Du'gal at the Altar of Blessings in Amani'Zar to begin worshipping Dundun.>

passages.title: Early Morning Training
passages.text: Great effort. Return next week for your continued training.

passages.title: Early Morning Training
passages.text:
Interested in enrolling in a training program? Some of the strongest warriors have emerged from hard work and dedication. 

With some practice, <name>, you surely can join their ranks. Begin today!

passages.title: Early Morning Training
passages.text: You have yet to finish your training for the week.

passages.title: Late Night Training: Week 1 of 3
passages.text: The hard work is paying off I see - great job! Return back to me next week.

passages.title: Late Night Training: Week 1 of 3
passages.text: Welcome back to this multi-course training - only a few weeks left! Let's put into practice what you learned last week. Go and participate in Battlegrounds in the Training Grounds or against other combatants, then return back to me.

passages.title: Late Night Training: Week 1 of 3
passages.text: You have yet to finish your training for the week.

passages.title: Midnight Training: Week 2 of 3
passages.text: Take note of what you've learned and prepare for your final training.

passages.title: Midnight Training: Week 2 of 3
passages.text: You're over half way done with your training! Again, let's take some of the lessons you have learned previously and apply them in the battle fields. Enter Training Grounds or Battlegrounds then return to me.

passages.title: Midnight Training: Week 2 of 3
passages.text: You have yet to finish your training for the week.

passages.title: Final Training: Week 3 of 3
passages.text: Well done completing the training program. For your hard work, take this! As you continue your journeys in battle, you can return back to me to become better equipped.

passages.title: Final Training: Week 3 of 3
passages.text: This is the final week of training. Take all of the lessons you've learned and put them into practice in the Training Grounds or against other players. Once complete, speak with Captain Dawnrunner in Falconwing Square.

passages.title: Blessings of Peril
passages.text:
An Idol of Peril...

Many shy away from de realm of perils. There is much danger surroundin' de immense power Puul blesses their worshippers with.

Will you risk your life for it?

passages.title: Blessings of Peril
passages.text:
<This idol proves the depth of your bond with peril.

Speak with Du'gal at the Altar of Blessings in Amani'Zar to begin worshipping Puul.>

passages.title: Blessings of The Depths
passages.text:
Jeju passed his Idol of de Depths on, did he?

There are not many souls willin' to brave de world beneath our ocean waves. But Pahk watches over all who surrender themselves to de currents--alive or otherwise.

passages.title: Blessings of The Depths
passages.text:
<This idol proves the depth of your bond with the Depths.

Speak with Du'gal at the Altar of Blessings in Amani'Zar to begin worshipping Pahk.>

passages.title: Preparations Underway
passages.text:
<Grayson examines the barding.>

This is... well, a good start, Highlord. But I think it will have to be strengthened a bit.

passages.title: Preparations Underway
passages.text:
As you may or may not recall, I once helped young paladins obtain their first armored mount.

It was a tedious task that involved months of obtaining materials and sending them all over Azeroth.

Thankfully, times have changed and we now have most of those materials at hand. That being said, I wish to help you obtain a new mount, something worthy of your title as Highlord.

In order for us to begin, I only require that you obtain a barding for us. Something strong, thick, and heavy.

passages.title: If You Build It
passages.text:
Excellent. This Unbending Potion should shore up the Felslate enough to hold the portal's structure, and these Chaotic Spinel crystals should focus the portal's magic nicely.

I will set the mo'arg to work posthaste.

passages.title: If You Build It
passages.text:
If we wish to achieve a sustained connection to Xoroth, we'll need a particularly resilient portal. Unfortunately, we can't just summon this one up from the ground.

I will need you to gather the requisite materials. Once we have them, I will have the mo'arg begin construction at once. 

Here's the list of what you'll need.

passages.title: It Takes Two
passages.text:
It was a dangerous trek back, but I made it in one piece.

I've been tellin' my uncle about our adventure. He loves a good story.

passages.title: It Takes Two
passages.text:
Jan'alai is a hen! And dat means eggs!

De eggs of de loa are volatile! Dey must be hatched carefully. My family carried dis honor for generations, but de tradition died when my older brothers followed de false promises of Zul'jin. Sadly, I am de only brother left, and we need two hatchers for de ritual!

Find my niece, Shaja, down by de shore. She is too young to know de ritual, but de loa's favor flows through her veins as it did my brothers'. It is time for her to know this honor.

passages.title: Hungry Hungry Hatchlings
passages.text: <Hopefully this will be enough food for the hatchlings.>

passages.title: Hungry Hungry Hatchlings
passages.text:
We will soon be blessed with eggs! Jan'alai has told me so. And once dem eggs hatch, we'll have many hungry mouths to feed! Dey will crave somethin' soft, delicate, and pungent.

<Brek eyes you up and down.>

Ya best scurry down to de shore and find somethin' to tempt de hatchlings with or dey may take a nibble out of you!

<Brek laughs.>

passages.title: Hungry Hungry Hatchlings
passages.text: <It's going to take ages to get this smell out of your armor.>

passages.title: Eggstra Protection Never Hurts
passages.text:
Ah ha! De feathers!

Dey will protect ya during de hatchin' ritual, but we must work a little magic on ya first. I taught Shaja the protection blessin' while you were runnin' about.

Do not worry! She is a natural.

<Brek grins wildly.>

passages.title: Eggstra Protection Never Hurts
passages.text:
De eggs are nearly ready!

<Brek glances eagerly at both clutches of eggs.>

Ya may know somethin' about dis, eh? Jan'alai tells me so. What ya lack in blood, ya make up for in spirit. Help me teach Shaja! Ya spirit alone is not enough for dis ritual. De eggs are imbued with de power of de loa herself and will burst with fiery energy!

We can protect ya from dis, but first we need feathers. Loa feathers! Collect dem from around de temple... unless ya dare ask de loa herself!

passages.title: Eggstra Protection Never Hurts
passages.text: Ya got de feathers? Or are ya gonna melt?

passages.title: Perfect Timing
passages.text:
The hatchin' is complete! Hopefully de first of many clutches to come. Jan'alai be praised!

Shaja and I will carry on dis legacy and welcome many new hatchlings to our land.

passages.title: Perfect Timing
passages.text:
All is ready! I will now guide ya both through de hatchin' ceremony!

Talk to Shaja and she will use de feathers to protect ya from dem powerful loa energies.

passages.title: Perfect Timing
passages.text: Hurry! Dem eggs are ready to pop!

passages.title: Like Dragonhawks to a Flame
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>. And Jan'alai thanks ya too.

I know dis is my path. By blood and by my own heart. I may never follow my mother into battle, but she will understand I serve de Amani--and Jan'alai--in my own way.

passages.title: Like Dragonhawks to a Flame
passages.text:
I know my uncle can seem... off at times. His talk of de loa always felt like childhood stories to me.

But ever since Jan'alai returned, I feel her energy too! She flickers, she smolders, she burns red hot. She also brings warmth, light, and life!

But what I feel from her right now is distress--dat of a mother hen counting her chicks but comin' up short.

Let's check on de hatchlings. We can cover more ground if we split up.

passages.title: Like Dragonhawks to a Flame
passages.text: We should keep lookin' around.

passages.title: Blessings of Pestilence
passages.text:
Many dread Mot'amra. And they aren't wrong to.

But pestilence, disease, death--these are natural occurrences. Those dat brave their own fear unlock de powerful understandin' of how to cure--or manipulate--these forces.

passages.title: Blessings of Pestilence
passages.text:
<This idol proves the depth of your bond with pestilence.

Speak with Du'gal at the Altar of Blessings in Amani'Zar to begin worshipping Mot'amra.>

passages.title: Blessings of Growth
passages.text:
My, my... is dis de idol of growth?

Oe is a loa very few know of or worship. They do not form their presence. Instead, they communicate through their domain of de forests, de plants, de world beneath our feet.

Tales from our first ancestors make it seem dat Oe followed de Amani from ancient Zandalar. Dat it chose us from all de other tribes when we were still young.

passages.title: Blessings of Growth
passages.text:
<This idol proves the depth of your bond with growth.

Speak with Du'gal at the Altar of Blessings in Amani'Zar to begin worshipping Oe.>

passages.title: Hal'hadar Battery Core
passages.text:
What troubles me is the timing of these attacks. Why now?

Are they allied with the Void... or simply taking advantage of the chaos left in the smoldering wake of Xal'atath's assault?

I cannot say for sure but perhaps there are others who can.

passages.title: Hal'hadar Battery Core
passages.text:
<The Hal'hadar battery core has been damaged, exposing its inner workings.

Amidst the thin energy wires and familiar metalwork seen in K'areshi technology, you spot gleaming yellow crystals fitted into a golden frame. Small runic letters on the metal are inscribed under it.

Perhaps one of the ethereals in the Howling Ridge in the Voidstorm could help identify this.>

passages.title: Hal'hadar Battery Core
passages.text:
I may not have fought these ethereals like Baraat has, but I am quite familiar with their technology. I decoded many of their encrypted schematics taken from the field.

Their use of technomancy and arcanic formula is quite advanced.

passages.title: Bindings of the Windlord
passages.text: And so you return with the bindings in hand. The Firelord shall be very displeased to have lost these.

passages.title: Bindings of the Windlord
passages.text:
With Thunderaan risen again as the lord of Skywall, there may indeed be an arrangement you can make in exchange for those wretched implements. But one binding is of no use on its own.

Return to me with both bindings, and with powerful enough ore to bind them, and I will arrange your audience with Thunderaan the Windlord.

passages.title: Bindings of the Windlord
passages.text: Yes, <race>?

passages.title: Lessons in the Void
passages.text: I'm glad you've chosen to join me here, <name>.

passages.title: Lessons in the Void
passages.text:
Ah, you're there!

Our esteemed Magister Umbric has tasked me with wrangling an able-bodied champion to assist him. An apprentice of his, Leona Darkstrider, is investigating the techniques and methods of the illidari.

It appears her inquiries may have put her in a bit of trouble.

The Magister can fill you in. He's in K'aresh now, and he's allowed me to open the way for you if you require transportation.

passages.title: A Bond of Brothers
passages.text: Another snake burrow. We must clear a path forward to find Jabat!

passages.title: A Bond of Brothers
passages.text:
My brother Tekkan and I were part of a team. Our friend Kariz died fighting de snakes.

Kariz's younger brother, Jabat, was consumed by vengeance. He is young and hot-headed, blind to his actions. He took off to kill de snakes. He is in great danger.

The Right Spear doesn't want to send a rescue, and I won't let their mother cry twice. We are going to get Jabat.

We need to plan an escape route for when we find Jabat. Tekkan can handle snake burrows with his explosives, but we need a muscle. You in?

passages.title: Too Quiet on the Northern Front
passages.text:
I... I don't know what happened there. I am sorry, <name>.

With de burrows and de reinforcements gone, dat snake over there... dat is the one who killed... Kariz.

passages.title: Too Quiet on the Northern Front
passages.text:
I only have one small explosive left. Even if Aol'ggin is right about my methods, we can't go back now. I...

<Tekkan chokes on his words, then clears his throat.>

We can do dis. You lure de snakes out and deal with dem so I can safely blow up de burrow. De escape route will be cleared after dat.

passages.title: Saving Recruit Jabat
passages.text:
Too many friends died down dis ravine. My brother Tekkan and de others...

<Aol'ggin shakes his head.>

Dey are sitting with de loa now.

One day Jabat and I will join dem. But not today.

passages.title: Saving Recruit Jabat
passages.text:
That large snake was the one who killed Kariz. And now I see Jabat is wounded and in danger. Tekkan is not responsive. I don't know what is wrong with him. There is no time to waste and I don't want to ask what else can go wrong. Dis is bad luck.

Check on Jabat or take out de large snake right away. Whatever you decide to do first, dat large snake must die.

passages.title: Darkspear Dash
passages.text:
You made it <name>! Ya feel all right, mon?

Time ta celebrate. We all be here together now!

passages.title: Darkspear Dash
passages.text:
Today, celebrate da Darkspear footrunners. 

Long ago, our footrunners ran 'round all da troll empire deliverin' important messages. Dey carried their messages through battle an' storm an' were famous for dey courage. 

Today we be celebratin' not dey courage in war, but da courage of some of da messages dey carried--messages of peace an' hope for a better world.

Help us send a message of hope by joinin' our symbolic run ta Silvermoon. 

Ya be ready? Well go, mon!

passages.title: War of Light and Shadow
passages.text: We have held the line with blood and Light. Now, we strike back.

passages.title: War of Light and Shadow
passages.text:
The Vanguard has begun to rally its forces to confront the Devouring Host.

Report to Lady Liadrin at the Sunwell to join the offensive.

passages.title: War of Light and Shadow
passages.text: The Devouring Host tried to break us. Soon, they will face the combined might of the Vanguard.

passages.title: Adventuring in Midnight
passages.text: You have embarked on a campaign chapter using the Scouting Map. You may return to the Sanctum of Light to make another selection.

passages.title: Adventuring in Midnight
passages.text: The Void encroaches on Azeroth from all sides. Visit the Scouting Map in the Sanctum of Light and choose where you will make your stand.

passages.title: Adventuring in Midnight
passages.text:
It's rare that we get to choose our paths in life, but you seem like someone who's seen it all before.

<Soridormi winks.>

Don't dally, this war won't win itself. Go to the Sanctum of Light. Choose where you'll make your first stand.

passages.title: Doing the Dash
passages.text:
You're welcome here, <class>.

Come celebrate with us for de race. You not gonna wanna miss it!

passages.title: Doing the Dash
passages.text:
Have you heard about the race today?

Thousands of trolls are gathering to run to Silvermoon City for a celebration!

Kalaya could tell you more. They're setting up at the Echo Isles now!

passages.title: Prey: Janoa the Fang (Nightmare)
passages.text:
This creature has established a reputation for particularly vicious ambushes. Envenomed fangs flashing in the dark, followed by frenzied thrashing and then... stillness. 

See if you cannot give it a taste of its own venom.

passages.title: Prey: Kursak the Coiled (Nightmare)
passages.text:
Do not let this serpentine monstrosity get close, adventurer, lest you have the life squeezed out of you. My servants recently found one of its unfortunate victims.

Like a fistful of mashed grapes...

Apologies, I lost myself for a moment there.

passages.title: Prey: Batani the Scaled (Nightmare)
passages.text:
I have heard that this creature has scales so thick and sharp you could use them to filet a fish. Do not let its diminutive stature fool you, adventurer, it was bred for one purpose. 

To kill. 

Fortunately, not being killed is something you've grown quite proficient in.

passages.title: Prey: Kadani the Claw (Nightmare)
passages.text: The claw! A miracle of the natural world. An appendage located at the cutting edge of murderous millennia. This creature is all claw and cunning, and you would do best to not fall prey to its violent nature.

passages.title: Torn Twilight Missive
passages.text:
The Twilight's Blade may be a minor thorn compared to the rampant domanaar or the ethereals attacking Quel'Thalas, but they are still dangerous.

If we can cut the heads off these snakes, then perhaps what little remains of them can finally dissipate into oblivion.

Continue the fight and keep up the good work, <name>.

passages.title: Torn Twilight Missive
passages.text:
<The Twilight Missive reads:

"Our search presses on yet we remain as divided as ever. If we don't unite, then we truly deserved to be abandoned by her!

Of our surviving Speakers, two refuse my missives.

Lazaar rallies survivors in the ruins of Deatholme, while Ger'lock amasses a host at the Broken Throne.

The others have yet to declare for them, which buys us time to continue our search.

We may yet salvage our broken cause."

The Ranger Captain will want to see this.>

passages.title: Torn Twilight Missive
passages.text: How fares your fight against the void assaults?

passages.title: Permafrosted Keystone
passages.text:
A keystone for a Burning Legion world in the possession of the domanaar is... concerning to say the least.

Until we know which world this once connected to, there's not much we can do.

Perhaps Allari and her new pupil will be able to reveal more about this void relic. I will send word to her and share what you have found.

Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: Permafrosted Keystone
passages.text:
<Several void-touched runes flicker across the keystone's surface before dissipating one by one. As the last rune fades, so does the faint hum of power within, leaving nothing but a painfully cold sphere of dark green metal.> 

Although it doesn't resemble other domanaar artifacts, there was no mistaking the cold, dark magic.

Perhaps Decimus in the Howling Ridge can provide you with more information.>

passages.title: Enchanted Naga Scroll
passages.text:
You were wise to bring this scroll to me.

I have more questions than answers... who sent this? And who is Nar'jira?

These new Deeplurk naga will only amplify the Daggerspine threat.

I will ensure the Ranger General is made aware of their presence.

Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: Enchanted Naga Scroll
passages.text:
<The enchanted scroll shimmers with an arcane glint, the text vaguely resembling the elven language.

You presume it is written in the language of the naga, though the arcane-laced ink appears to move the letters around the scroll.

Perhaps a mage in Silvermoon can help you translate it.>

passages.title: Enchanted Naga Scroll
passages.text: Yes, <name>?

passages.title: Prey: A Crimson Summons
passages.text:
Look at you.... following directions already. 

Excellent.

passages.title: Prey: A Crimson Summons
passages.text:
Ah, adventurer. I have been looking for you. My... contacts have told me much regarding your continued attempts to defend our beloved city.

But there is another way.

Come, join me in Murder Row and we can get to work.

passages.title: A New Direction
passages.text:
I'm glad you selected your second-in-command, <name>.

But Stormwind mourns today, and we must act.

passages.title: A New Direction
passages.text:
<Your hand burns with felfire as a scroll materializes within your grasp. The seal bears the mark of the Illidari.>

<name>, as leader of the Illidari in Lord Illidan's absence, you must choose your second-in-command.

Kayn or Altruis. You can only choose one.

The chosen shall become your personal champion, and their ideology will color our decisions for the Illidari going forward. No matter who is chosen, our mission remains unchanged.

-Kor'vas Bloodthorn

passages.title: The Venomous Abyss: Deception Unmasked
passages.text: If my brother is no longer bowing to Malacrass, then he's in grave danger. We need to find a way to get to dem as quickly as possible. Look for anything that could let us get through de temple faster.

passages.title: The Venomous Abyss: Deception Unmasked
passages.text: If my brother is no longer bowing to Malacrass, then he's in grave danger. We need to find a way to get to dem as quickly as possible. Look for anything that could let us get through de temple faster.

passages.title: Bring the Ruckus
passages.text:
This place is pretty fun so far, despite all the dry political talk. I know Saltheril is trying to get the nobles to buy up war bonds, but we could really use some more energy in here. If the nobles are all asleep, no one's buying anything.

Tell you what. Go invite some of my friends. They hang out under the bridge right outside of Silvermoon's gates.

If anyone can bring some energy to the soiree, it's us.

passages.title: Bring the Ruckus
passages.text:
The energy's high, the drinks are flowing, and people are having a good time!

That's how you start making deals.

passages.title: One Smuggler to Another
passages.text:
The whole point of this deal is showing the nobles what we bring to the table, both for Silvermoon and for them personally.

These other groups bring strength, power, and really nice armor. What we bring is resources: getting the sin'dorei what they need, when they need it, with no questions asked.

I heard some folks over at Sunsail Anchorage have been trying out the same business, but they're putting gold in the wrong pockets. Swipe their stock and bring it here.

passages.title: One Smuggler to Another
passages.text: I don't mind competitors, but I don't like the deals those smugglers are making.

passages.title: One Smuggler to Another
passages.text: If there's anything good in these crates, we'll get it on the market.

passages.title: Dangerous Showpieces
passages.text:
You'd be surprised at the money you can make off of weapons. No, not the kind you're meant to use--the kind you stick up on the wall and have conversations about.

Usually those weapons are expensive, or dangerous, or otherwise hard to get your hands on. The more rare and exclusive, the better.

The weapons those Twilight cultists are carrying around should sell pretty well, especially to buyers with edgier tastes. If you happen to come across any, I'll gladly take them off your hands.

passages.title: Dangerous Showpieces
passages.text: If it has some blood on it, that's actually better.

passages.title: Dangerous Showpieces
passages.text: Nice work. Eversong is safer because of your heroism, and I get to pocket a little more gold. I'd call that a win-win.

passages.title: Artisanal Replicas
passages.text:
Don't let the austere demeanor fool you. Nobles are just as susceptible to flashy party favors as the rest of us.

I had my people bring over a batch of Felo'melorn replicas. They look great on display, and even better--they're enchanted. Swing them around and they leave a trail of fire.

I haven't sold an enchanted batch before, so I'd like to do some testing before I hand them out. Saltheril wouldn't be too happy if I burned a guest to a crisp.

Wanna take one of the replicas for a test run?

passages.title: Artisanal Replicas
passages.text:
I recommend trying it out on something not flammable.

Or extremely flammable. Up to you.

passages.title: Artisanal Replicas
passages.text:
I told you they were flashy!

Sounds like the enchantment could get tuned down a little bit, but where's the fun in that?

passages.title: Shady Dealings
passages.text:
I feel like I just got here and I'm already fresh out of half the poisons I brought.

What? Don't look at me like that. Nobles are some of my top customers for poisons. Quieter than magic and cleaner than blades.

I need to restock. The frogs way down in the south produce a poisonous slime that I can bottle without much fuss. Bring some of it to me and I'll get you a cut of the earnings.

passages.title: Shady Dealings
passages.text: Were you able to find any of those frogs?

passages.title: Shady Dealings
passages.text:
Excellent. That's enough to restock what I've sold and then some.

Oh, by the way, you probably want to wash your hands. Maybe a few times.

passages.title: Throw the Dice
passages.text:
We've been making friends with some of the guests by teaching them how to play dice. It's a nice way to draw people out of the crowd and get them in a quieter space where you can talk privately.

I wasn't expecting so much interest, to be honest. We're running out of dice sets.

I can carve some more, but I'll need materials. Usually teeth or bone are good picks. Actually, the fangs from those naga along the coast would be perfect. Now that's a conversation starter!

passages.title: Throw the Dice
passages.text: Any luck finding some of those fangs?

passages.title: Throw the Dice
passages.text:
Oh, that smell is... very fishy. Definitely going to let these dry out for a while.

Your exceptionally efficient help is appreciated, <name>.

passages.title: We Need a Refill
passages.text:
I talked to some of the servants earlier and it sounds like the casks are running low. That's a recipe for disaster at an event like this.

Fortunately, I've got a lot of contacts across Eversong who can help us restock.

I need to stay here and play politics, but could you head over to Tranquillien and grab a few bottles? I'll give you a list.

passages.title: We Need a Refill
passages.text: Trust me. Everything on that list is fantastic.

passages.title: We Need a Refill
passages.text: Nice work. I'll see about getting those casks refilled, but these bottles should keep everyone happy in the meantime.

passages.title: Begged, Borrowed, or Stolen
passages.text:
The oldest trick in the book is to create a problem on purpose, solve it yourself, and look like the hero.

One of the nobles just got word that some prized valuable was stolen from their estate while they were occupied here. It just so happens I might have put one of their servants up to it.

Go talk to a man named Seridis over at the livery. He'll hand over the valuable to you, then you'll come back here and pretend you valiantly subdued the thief and retrieved the item.

Everyone's happy.

passages.title: Begged, Borrowed, or Stolen
passages.text: Making friends with the servants in noble households opens up a lot of doors. Sometimes literally.

passages.title: Begged, Borrowed, or Stolen
passages.text:
Look at that. Everyone comes out a winner!

The noble gets his valuable back unscathed, Seridis gets paid handsomely, and you and I look brave and capable in front of the soiree.

passages.title: WANTED: Gorebarb's Pincers
passages.text:
Gorebarb is a creature quite unlike most others who make Harandar their home. He's incredibly violent and his kind is not seen here very often. 

Let's see less of him. Kill him and bring me his pincers as proof of the deed.

passages.title: WANTED: Gorebarb's Pincers
passages.text: Take care that Gorebarb doesn't catch you with those pincers. I imagine his breath isn't pleasant at all.

passages.title: WANTED: Gorebarb's Pincers
passages.text: Well, well. You managed to take down Gorebarb and retrieve the pincers? Ah, of course I never doubted you would.

passages.title: WANTED: Dionaea's Thorntusks
passages.text:
Many thornmaws make the mire their home, but none as are vicious as Dionaea. Unlike the others, she kills merely for the joy of it, and her gluttony threatens the delicate balance of the wildlife in this area. 

Take her out and restore the equilibrium. Bring me back her thorntusks as proof of the deed.

passages.title: WANTED: Dionaea's Thorntusks
passages.text: Dionaea hunts for the thrill of it. She seems to be unable to satiate her hunger. Have you handled her yet?

passages.title: WANTED: Dionaea's Thorntusks
passages.text: You bring me the thorntusks? Excellent. May balance return to the Mire.

passages.title: A New Tradition
passages.text:
Chon was just looking for you. You can find him at his house, serving drinks with Chen.

<Lorewalker Cho laughs--a deep, warm rumble.>

Go on, adventurer! I won't be leaving anytime soon, that's for sure.

passages.title: A New Tradition
passages.text:
Ah, <name>... you have traveled far, but returned. You have reminded all who live here that the Spirit Festival is not just for the elemental spirits, but the spirits of all <race> who call this place home... even if they leave for a time. 

In thanks, our tailors have crafted these for you. The maker's design celebrates your adventures, but also honors your origins... just as you have today.

Master Shang Xi would be so, so proud.

To you, my friend. To home.

passages.title: Meet the Vandals
passages.text: <The Manaforge Vandals at Shadow Point are eager to see the Shadowguard and their allies removed from Manaforge Omega. It's probably a good time to pay them a visit.>

passages.title: Meet the Vandals
passages.text: Hero! Your reputation for toppling tyrants precedes you. Let's see about adding one more to that list.

passages.title: Ignite the Skies: Northern Kalimdor
passages.text:
Midsummer is the time to reflect and a time to tell stories by the bonfire.

One such story is the tale of the sun blossom ritual and how this offering to An'she first came to be.

Our journey will take us through Northern Kalimdor, into territories beyond the lands of the shu'halo.

If you wish, take to the skies of Kalimdor and ignite the blossoms as I tell the tale.

Our story begins in the Western Barrens...

passages.title: Ignite the Skies: Northern Kalimdor
passages.text:
This important journey would soon become a yearly pilgrimage for the tribes of Central Kalimdor.

As the summer season approached, and the tribes began to gather near Stonetalon, a chosen few would journey to the highest peak and make offerings to the sun.

An'she was pleased by this act, and the offering of sun blossoms became pivotal to Midsummer celebration.

passages.title: Infusion of Hope
passages.text:
I hope my staff's light has been enough to uphold those at the Sunwell while we have sought these relics.

Together with those from Light's Hope, they should be a much more significant aid.

Let us return there quickly.

passages.title: Infusion of Hope
passages.text: Quickly, <name>. Let us get these distributed!

passages.title: It Follows Me
passages.text:
You must listen. An evil creature attached itself to me not long ago. It followed me about, angrily hurling objects, playing tricks, and consuming anything it could.

Just now, it stopped following me. It likes you now, I think.

If you feed it, it should leave you be for a time. Mark the defeated in the Sparring Grounds with this brand. It should consume them, giving us time to talk more.

passages.title: It Follows Me
passages.text:
It's still hungry. The meals are never enough.

That's why I'm so weakened. It was constantly nagging me. You seem strong enough, though.

passages.title: One Hero's Prey
passages.text:
Again, we sin'dorei find our city under assault. And again, it is up to the finer minds among us to come to Silvermoon's aid.

Mortal anguish, it seems, is a powerful reflection of the soul. When contained and manipulated, anguish acts as a form of magic that we can wield to protect this great city.

I've located a number of anguish-filled targets across Azeroth.

Select and hunt one such target, storing their anguish in this crystalline vessel. Then return to me.

passages.title: One Hero's Prey
passages.text: While you collect more anguish, I will experiment with this power's potential.

passages.title: Practical Magic
passages.text:
While you've been out pursuing targets, I've been developing various applications for anguish.

The power these raw emotions contain is unfathomable. For now, our applications might seem quaint, but given enough time, I'm certain my discoveries will further Silvermoon's aims.

Let me show you. Take the crystalline vessel and meet me below.

passages.title: Practical Magic
passages.text:
For so many years, I've dedicated my life to these magical pursuits.

This next chapter will be something to behold.

passages.title: Dark Mending
passages.text:
So far, anguish has been invaluable in bolstering our forces. Our weaponry and golems are all the more hardy and potent thanks to this newfound power.

I've also been developing ways to shape anguish into robust enchantments that can strengthen us elves.

Meet me downstairs. I will show you what I've found.

passages.title: Dark Mending
passages.text: Unfortunate side effects are expected when we're on the bleeding edge of magical discoveries.

passages.title: Precious Jewels
passages.text:
<name>...

While you've been away, I've been refining our work.

<He produces a jeweled ring in the palm of his hand.>

Small trinkets and jewelry that contain crystallized anguish.

I've discretely gifted these to a few willing Silvermoon citizens. I wish to observe the effect of a controlled concentration of anguish over time.

I've shaped the magic to lend the bearer health and strength. Seek our volunteers out and check up on them.

passages.title: Precious Jewels
passages.text: My work here will make the world fear Silvermoon's might.

passages.title: Precious Jewels
passages.text:
Aggression is simply an expression of strength.

So long as we are the predator, not the prey.

passages.title: Garden Variety Sacrifices
passages.text:
<name>... I need you to attend to a matter in the city.

I've received word from Knight Captain Solara that there's been an incident in the Gardens of Remembrance. She reports elves have begun acting out violently, causing coalesced anguish to manifest and terrorize the residents.

You can use the crystalline vessel to reclaim the coalesced anguish and soothe the elves whose minds have crumbled.

So much of the magic will weigh heavy upon you, but I'm confident you have the strength.

passages.title: Garden Variety Sacrifices
passages.text: In all of my endeavors, there are always some who seek to impede my progress.

passages.title: Garden Variety Sacrifices
passages.text: There will always be some who resist progress, but no matter the cost, my studies in anguish are for the people of Silvermoon.

passages.title: The Sheep or the Wolf
passages.text:
I heard word of your heroics in the garden. Silvermoon thanks you for quelling the chaos.

And I thank you for recovering so much anguish.

The crystalline vessel may be the conduit, but the body must be robust to handle so much power... Like me, you have the strength to withstand the torrent of anguish inside you, at least for a short while.

Come, let me relieve you of the burden.

passages.title: The Sheep or the Wolf
passages.text:
Anguish is power, and power is predation.

Would you rather that we be the sheep or the wolf?

passages.title: The Tale of the Frost Lord
passages.text:
Midsummer is the time to reflect on the past and share stories by the fireside.

One such tale is the defeat of Frost Lord Ahune!

But this is a story you must witness for yourself so you may share it around the bonfire with others!

passages.title: The Tale of the Frost Lord
passages.text:
Now that, my friend, is a story worth telling.

It is a tale we shaman often reflect upon during this time.

The stirring of the Frost Lord during the season of fire was an imbalance of nature. A flame that never should have sparked.

It is a cautionary tale of passion and conflict that we would all do well to remember.

Thank you for this reminder.

passages.title: Hagar's Invitation
passages.text:
Hagar has a message she believes the elves and trolls of Azeroth must all hear. She has sent a call to leaders from the elven and troll tribes to come to Harandar.

I have come here to ask the blood elves to join us, but you should be there as well. You have been with us through so much of this.

The Rootways from Silvermoon would be the fastest way.

passages.title: Hagar's Invitation
passages.text: It should not be long now.

passages.title: The Preparations Are Complete
passages.text:
<name>,

I bear an important message from Hagar. You are invited to a special meeting in Harandar. Please meet me in Silvermoon to discuss it.

Orweyna

passages.title: The Preparations Are Complete
passages.text: The preparations have been made.

passages.title: History Lesson
passages.text:
Hagar requested that we invite to this meeting all of the troll and elven leaders we know.

It was not easy to convince them to come. There are some... past grievances between these groups. Hagar hopes to overcome these divisions.

As we wait for the others to arrive, feel free to speak to the other delegates. The wait is making them restless, so try not to inflame tensions.

passages.title: History Lesson
passages.text:
Good to see you again!

<Kinduru looks around the Den, then sighs.>

Do you know where Zul'jan has stomped off to?

passages.title: A Favor for Kinduru
passages.text:
Zul'jarra could not leave Zul'Aman as the Amani still recover. She sent Zul'jan in her stead.

She hoped showing trust and giving him dis responsibility would bring him out of her shadow. Make use of his talents. But dis news...

I am an old troll. I have a hard time reining Zul'jan in, but he may listen to you.

Would you join us? Zul'jarra and I would be grateful if Zul'jan stayed out of trouble.

passages.title: A Favor for Kinduru
passages.text: My patience is dwindling.

passages.title: Revisionist History
passages.text:
Not all of the visions in this place were clear to us. Some of them were... strange.

One in particular seemed to revolve around an unfamiliar people: a people that we learned are the Amani trolls.

The magic used to create the painting, to pull the memories from the past, are tied to the haranir and those close to us. If there was no connection, the Zur'ashar--who create the paintings--could not have recalled troll history.

I can show you and Zul'jan, and you can judge for yourselves.

passages.title: Revisionist History
passages.text: Amani history, painted on the walls of our ancestors. This magic does not work without a bond between our peoples.

passages.title: Return to Zul'Aman
passages.text:
I have heard de story since I was a child! De Amani were outnumbered and still dey fought on! Dey claimed victory through sheer will!

Orweyna says de visions cannot lie. Uncle thinks details of de battle could have been lost. Dey would question everything it means to be Amani.

<Zul'jan scowls.>

I must find de truth of dis. Uncle says if anyone would know, it would be de loa. De loa have said nothing of dis before, but we must start somewhere.

It's time to go home.

passages.title: Return to Zul'Aman
passages.text: Why is my uncle so disorganized?

passages.title: Help Uncle with Loa
Captain Tokka
passages.text: It be good to see some fresh faces around here. My crew and I have been stranded for over seven years, and we were beginning to believe we'd have to rebuild society from scratch!

passages.title: Captain Tokka
passages.text:
We'd been sailing Torga's Beak, a gift given to us by the Zandalari, when out of nowhere a great white serpent broke our hull. My crew acted quickly, and took us to shore before we took on too much water.

Would have been better to let the ship sink and swim back to Zul'Aman, but little did we know the trap we had put ourselves in.

After establishing ourselves on the island, we built small dinghies to escape--only to find the fogs constantly turning us back to shore.

We've spent the last few years making this place a home. We had begun to acclimate, until just a day ago when the foul serpents poured forth from the mountainside. My crew scattered across this cursed island.

What cruel winds, for the fog to lift only now.

passages.title: Captain Tokka
passages.text:
'Twas a cursed land, even before the snakes emerged. Many a crewmate found themselves attacked by the souls of the dead that wander here, and we've found a number of other Zandalari ships that met the fate of ours.

To the north, we've made allies with a hermit by the name of Ofi, an Amani exile. She prefers to keep to herself, but is the only friendly face we've seen.

To the east, the island turns to muck and mud, and a combination of murlocs and spirits make their home there. The murlocs have a crazed glint in their eyes... a curse that spread to some of my crewmates as well. As for the spirits, some of them seem friendly enough while others attack you on sight. We've generally found it best to avoid the dead.

passages.title: Captain Tokka
passages.text:
To the south lays Gnarldor Isle, where some burly giants seem to have taken home. They're none too friendly and we give them a wide berth.

To the west are the crypts and temples where the snakes emerged from. My crew is a superstitious sort and don't like messing with graves, so we thought to leave the quiet lands alone. We didn't expect venom to spew from the mountains and flying snakes with two heads!

You'd best be getting on with your soldiers. I could use your help around here later, but for now it seems we have an outpost to fortify.

You're a ray of hope, Nerfwins.

passages.title: The Blooming Lattice
passages.text:
You're that stranger I've been hearing about, aren't you? I'm Su'meera, apprentice painter to Ja'kul. You heard of him? No? Maybe his work hasn't made it to your lands. That makes sense, I guess.

Anyhow, I heard you like helping people out. Well, a few important things went missing when Ja'kul was attacked and killed. I want them back.

Will you meet me near Blooming Lattice?

passages.title: Supplicants to the Goddess
passages.text:
We have long tended to the roots with the help of the creatures who live and grow here. Think of it as a symbiotic relationship from which we, the creatures, and the roots all benefit. That said, my partner Riverscale isn't contributing very much lately!

Please help me find a way to motivate him again.

First, you must cleanse off the essence of the outside. Cleanse yourself in the waters of Har'kuai.

passages.title: Midnight: World Tour
passages.text: Back so soon? Impressive!

passages.title: Forged Through Fire
passages.text:
It is said the blessings of a phoenix long-forgotten seep through every swing of the hammer and bellow of flames at this forge.

That is why any who are serious about their craft come from all over to forge their creations here at this spot. Perhaps though, all that power is just superstition. A way for the Sunstrider dynasty to give power to the powerless. Yet again, perhaps it is not.

Give it a try, won't you?

passages.title: Lor'themar Theron
passages.text: Silvermoon is grateful for your aid.

passages.title: Vaultkeeper Elysa
passages.text: How may I help you?

passages.title: Silvermoon Guard
passages.text: What do you seek, priest?

passages.title: Eldara Dawnrunner
passages.text:
A sight to behold, is it not?

Since the time of Dath'Remar, the elves have used this great forge to craft armor of unparalleled might. It is said that the flames were first stoked by the soul of a phoenix who thought it a fitting nest, and that its power still weaves itself through every creation.

We will permit you to share in its gifts.

passages.title: Eldara Dawnrunner
passages.text: The Catalyst can infuse great power into items, enhancing them and pushing their potential further than ever before!

passages.title: Theremis
passages.text: Which Midnight Specialization would you like to relearn?

passages.title: Dolothos
passages.text: Greetings. Are you seeking instruction in enchanting?

passages.title: Camberon
passages.text: Greetings. Are you seeking instruction in alchemy?

passages.title: Greenspeaker Cyenna
passages.text:
We are blessed to live in Harandar, and we treat that as a responsibility. The roots of World Trees wind through these lands, and we must tend to them to make sure that they continue to thrive.

I am Cyenna, Charge Nurse of Nordrassil. It is a responsibility I take very seriously.

passages.title: Ranger Telenus
passages.text:
Train a dog, I said. How hard could it be, I said. 

I need to stop talking.

passages.title: Loa Speaker Yl'mul
passages.text: All that's left here is me and de captain. De curse I cast keeps us from movin' on.

passages.title: Silvermoon Guard
passages.text: What do you seek, priest?

passages.title: Witherbark Cook
passages.text: The ingredients I've got are... suspicious at best. Eh, with your help I'm sure it'll be at least edible.

passages.title: Profaned Plaque
passages.text: I have seen such horrors in life. I commit myself to an everlasting death to save my children and their children from the evil that defeated darkness. The snakes must remain sealed away. The weapon is as deadly as the Void. Our shame must remained buried. I proudly pay the eternal price. Let my spirit guard these halls. Let my shade bar the way.

passages.title: Profaned Plaque
passages.text: Let my spirit guard these halls. Let my shade bar the way. Let no Ah-mah-nee or trespassing thief cross the threshold. Zaz'ke the Guardian.

passages.title: Message in a Bottle
passages.text: Help! Our ship, Sethraliss's Scale, has run aground. We are on an island east of Zul'Aman. Send help and you can have the cargo we saved. Captain Lenta.

passages.title: Message in a Bottle
passages.text: The bottle came back. Again. I've thrown it out to sea on the tide. This makes no sense. If you find this, tell a tortollan sailor. They will know who I am. We still have plenty of cargo to reward you if you come and rescue us. Captain Lenta.

passages.title: Message in a Bottle
passages.text: This bottle won't stop returning. This island is haunted and infested with snakes. We would still like to be rescued, but I understand if you stay far away from here. All we have found are wrecks of Zandalari ships. I should never have purchased a Zandalari ship. Whatever has cursed this island does not like the Zandalari. Can't it see I'm a tortollan? I hope this bottle floats away this time. Captain Lenta.

passages.title: Message in a Bottle
passages.text: Captain Lenta was bitten by a snake. Don't come here. This island is a cage. Swabby Wuck.
